Home.closingTitle: Each article needs a source and a reviewer.
Home.closingBody: The catalogue lists topics. Before an article can serve as a reference, it needs a named edition, a precise page or verse, notes on differences among traditions, and review by someone qualified.

Start.metadataDescription: Follow reading paths on ahimsa, karma, liberation, Jain cosmology, texts, and communities. Linked topic articles are currently in English.
Start.title: Start with a question.
Start.lead: Each path links related topics and questions. Follow the order shown or open any topic that interests you. These pages explain ideas; they do not give religious instructions.
Start.topicLanguageNote: Path titles and linked topic articles are in English. Opening a topic takes you to its English draft.

paths.title: An introduction to Jain traditions
paths.description: Read a short introduction, learn what ahimsa means, and note where Jain communities give different accounts.
questions: Which ideas do Jain communities share, and where do their accounts differ?
How do knowledge, ethics, and spiritual effort connect?

paths.title: Soul, karma, and liberation
paths.description: Read how Jain traditions describe the soul, karma, and release from rebirth.
questions: What does it mean in Jain philosophy to describe karma as subtle matter?
Why is a favorable rebirth still different from liberation?

paths.title: The Jain cosmos and the wheel of time
paths.description: Read about loka and aloka and Jain accounts of the universe and time. These are religious teachings, not models of modern astronomy.
questions: What belongs within loka, and how is aloka described?
What do the six eras explain in Jain cosmology?

paths.title: Ahimsa, restraint, and many-sided understanding
paths.description: Read about ahimsa and Jain vows, then consider how anekantavada approaches disagreement.
questions: How do mendicant vows differ from lay vows?
How can different standpoints help clarify a disagreement without treating every claim as equally true?

paths.title: Jain stories, memory, and history
paths.description: Read stories of Rishabha, Bahubali, Mahavira, and Malli. Separate their place in Jain tradition from claims historians can assess with evidence.
questions: What does a story teach within Jain tradition, and what can historical evidence establish?
How should differing accounts of Malli be presented?

paths.title: Texts, teachers, and living communities
paths.description: Read how Jain teachings were preserved and passed on. Compare how Jain communities describe their texts and community life.
questions: Why do Jain communities preserve different accounts of their scriptural canons?
How do monks, nuns, laywomen, and laymen form the fourfold community?

Editorial.metadataDescription: Learn how this Jain study library labels drafts, records sources, describes differences, and checks articles before review.
Editorial.title: Read. Then check the source.
Editorial.lead: This independent study project introduces Jain traditions. Most articles still need source checks and review by qualified readers.
Editorial.draftCopy: No qualified reviewer has checked every claim in these articles. The source lists do not name a verifiable edition and exact page or verse. Use the summaries as an introduction while review is incomplete.
Editorial.reviewedHeading: What a reviewed article will show
reviewedPoints: The source title, edition or translation, and exact chapter, verse, page, or section.
Whether a claim comes from a Jain text, traditional commentary, community teaching, or academic research.
Interpretations and disagreements by tradition, instead of one account presented as every Jain’s view.
The reviewer’s name, relevant experience, and review date. A citation alone is not verification.
sourceDescriptions: A short secondary source for initial orientation.
A Svetambara account of textual transmission and differing canons.
One scholarly argument about historical evidence; it is not a universal consensus.
Editorial.reviewCallout: Early review should focus on introductory topics, ethics, texts, and articles that mention fasting or sallekhana. Detailed guidance in these areas needs qualified human review first.

Practice.title: Prayers and observances
Practice.description: Prayer and observance differ among Jain communities. These pages are drafts; their texts and translations still need to be checked against named sources.

entries.title: Navkar Mantra
entries.description: A Jain salutation. Its text, transliteration, and interpretation need a specific textual and community context.

entries.title: Chattari Mangalam
entries.description: A verse naming auspicious refuges in some Jain liturgies; wording and use vary by context.

entries.title: Logassa Sutra
entries.description: A sutra associated with praise of the Tirthankaras. Its text and translation still need source checks.

entries.title: Bhaktamar Stotra
entries.description: A Sanskrit stotra in Jain devotional practice. Its authorship, textual variants, and translations need review.

entries.title: Uvasaggaharam Stotra
entries.description: A stotra associated with Pārśvanātha. Its text and interpretations need specific sources.

entries.title: Khamemi Savva Jive
entries.description: A verse about forgiveness. Its wording, occasion, and interpretation need community-specific sources.

entries.title: Pratikraman
entries.description: A practice of reflection and atonement, with forms that differ by community, lineage, and context.

entries.title: Paryushana and Das Lakshana
entries.description: Annual observances whose dates and practices differ among Jain communities.

Practice.context: These pages introduce selected observances. Practices differ among communities and individuals. Do not use this material to decide whether or how long to fast; it is not medical advice or religious authority.
Practice.entryHeading: Text and interpretation still need review
Practice.entryBody: This page is not yet a verified translation or ritual guide. A qualified reviewer still needs to check its text, wording, and tradition-specific context against named editions. Detailed passages and interpretations will be added after that review is recorded.
